theProblemWithTheInheritedBar.statement: The union-ratio bar is ILL-CONDITIONED on the dark poses.
theProblemWithTheInheritedBar.evidence: Source mean luminance is 0.201-0.216 at azimuth 55 and 0.038-0.042 at azimuth 235, a factor of five. A fixed RELATIVE bar admits five times less absolute error on the shadow side for no stated reason. At 4,000/235 an absolute difference of 0.0024 — among the smallest measured — is a 5.7% MISS, while 0.0087 at 400/55, over three times larger, is a 4.0% PASS.

A1.name: Relative tone, well-exposed poses only
A1.rationale: The inherited bar at its inherited value, applied only where a ratio is well conditioned. The 0.05 is NOT re-chosen.

A2.name: Absolute tone, every pose
A2.derivation: 0.05 * 0.21 = 0.0105 -> 0.010, what the inherited bar means in absolute terms on a well-exposed pose.
A2.fairnessFramingStatedHonestly: THIS IS NOT A NEUTRAL TRANSLATION. A fixed absolute bar is LOOSER in relative terms exactly where the subject is dark: 0.010 permits about 25% relative error at the shadow poses (0.010/0.040) against 5% at the lit poses (0.010/0.210). It trades one bias for the opposite bias. The argument for it is that absolute light error is what a viewer perceives against a scene, not error relative to a locally dark denominator — but that is an argument, not a proof, and the asymmetry is stated rather than buried.

A3.name: Hue
A3.rule: max per-channel ratio spread <= 0.02 at EVERY pose.
A3.rationale: Unchanged from T002 and T010. Not re-chosen.

antiFittingStatement: NONE OF THESE NUMBERS WAS CHOSEN BY REFERENCE TO WHAT THE TILE SCORES. A1 and A3 are inherited unchanged; A2 is derived arithmetically from A1 at the lit reference; the luminance floor is half the lit level, a property of the two pose populations. Scores were computed AFTER the bars were written.

whatTheV1TileScores.note: REPORTED, NOT USED TO SET THE BARS.

FLAGGED_FOR_USER_DECISION.issue: THE CHOICE OF GATE FORM MATERIALLY DECIDES A VERDICT, so it is flagged rather than decided.
FLAGGED_FOR_USER_DECISION.detail: At 4,000/235 the tile MISSES the inherited relative bar (0.942736) and PASSES the derived absolute bar (0.002416 against 0.010). Adopting A2 converts the only surviving tone failure into a pass.
FLAGGED_FOR_USER_DECISION.whyItIsNotMineToDecide: A gate change that flips the one failing verdict must not be made by the party measuring it.
optionsForTheUser: Adopt A1 + A2 + A3 as proposed; 4,000/235 becomes a tone PASS and the open tone question closes.
Adopt A2 + A3 only, dropping the relative bar entirely as ill-conditioned.

MIDDLE OPTION: keep a RELATIVE bar at every pose but with an explicitly larger tolerance at dark poses — for example 0.05 where source mean >= 0.10 and a stated wider tolerance below it. This keeps the relative form, admits the conditioning problem openly, and forces the dark-pose tolerance to be argued as a number rather than inherited by accident. Under a 0.08 dark tolerance the tile would still MISS 4,000/235 at 0.0573; under 0.10 it would pass.
Keep the inherited relative bar at all poses and carry 4,000/235 as an open tone failure.
Adopt A1 + A2 + A3 but additionally REPORT the relative value at dark poses unbarred, so the deficit stays visible without gating on it.

hueIsIndependentOfThisDecision: A3 is unchanged and the tile misses it at five of six poses under every form considered. That failure needs an owner regardless.
